body:
**Summary**

We used to consider that when using `showMore`, you wouldn't use `searchForFacetValues`. Turns out it's been asked and even at Algolia we do so (latest example is the about page). This patch actually fixes the behavior so that both can work and that the end-user will be able to go from one to the other.

**Result**

fixes #2478 
fixes #3064

Scenario:
In a search with a refinement list that has both `showMore` and `searchForFacetValues` activated.
 - click on show more
 - type some search in the query (should hide the show more / show less button)
 - remove the query (should display the show more / show less button with the correct state)
 - toggle show less (should work)

Old implementation:
![2018-08-27 16 23 21](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/393765/44665385-0e41dd00-aa16-11e8-9aad-ac9adb6aabc0.gif)

Fixed implementation:
![2018-08-27 16 26 46](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/393765/44665394-169a1800-aa16-11e8-8978-6328695e8ebf.gif)

Initially my request was when searching for hits. It's when you change the input from the main search box that it breaks the refinementList.
@sylvain-h ok so that a different issue. Is it something easy to address @francoischalifour ?

The `toggleShowMore()` method cannot work when _searching for facet values_ as is because it re-renders the widget, and therefore loses the query in the search box.

Here's what I suggest:

- If you've started typing in the SFFV searchbox without having toggled "Show more", display `limit` results. Otherwise, display `showMoreLimit` results (fixes issue mentioned in @Haroenv's message).

- If there's no hits returned in the main search, hide the refinement list "Show more" button (fixes issue mentioned in @tkrugg's message).

I've implemented this behavior that you can test [in this story](https://deploy-preview-3082--instantsearchjs.netlify.com/stories/?selectedKind=RefinementList&selectedStory=with%20search%20and%20show%20more).

Can you confirm that's what we want to go for so I can unit test it fully?

@sylvain-h confirmed that this is the expected behavior.

We're good for review @algolia/instantsearch-for-websites.

@francoischalifour I see one last thing I think can be improved.

Since the latest fix, we have the following situation:
- if we have no refinements, the showMore/showLess button is hidden. This is perfect 👍 
- If I have less refinements than `limit`, the showMore button will not show more items. Similarly, the showLess button will not collapse the few refinements displayed.
As a results, theses buttons appear to be broken.

As a user I think it would make more sense that we hide them or disable them. What are your thoughts on that?
